claims.text: In situ TEM oxidation experiments can elucidate oxidation mechanisms and nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
The initial Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 material is additively manufactured and contains dual nanoprecipitation.
Oxidation can be investigated by in situ TEM at high temperature, exemplified by 800°C, in a controlled atmosphere.
Nanoprecipitates are the structural feature mediating the oxidation behavior under investigation.
In situ TEM enables real-time observation of oxidation behavior.
In situ TEM oxidation experiments enable observation of elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates.
The additively manufactured alloy will exhibit a 20% lower oxidation degradation rate than cast and wrought counterparts.
Oxidation degradation is quantified by weight gain per unit area after 100 hours of high-temperature exposure.
The comparator is cast and wrought Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
The proposed method and hypothesis apply to high-temperature applications above 500°C.
The oxidation degradation rate may depend on experimental conditions and the additively manufactured alloy's microstructure.
The hypothesis is falsified if oxidation degradation is not reduced by at least 15% relative to the cast and wrought baseline after 100 hours.
